extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary staff, and legal professionals interested in USPTO reciprocal disciplinary procedures
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 imposing reciprocal discipline (exclusion) on a registered patent practitioner based on disbarment in a state jurisdiction, and describing the procedural steps, authority, publication, and notice obligations tied to that discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may impose reciprocal discipline upon a practitioner identical to discipline imposed by a state bar (Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Notice and Order was mailed informing Respondent that the OED DGC had filed a Complaint requesting reciprocal discipline identical to the state-imposed discipline; reciprocal discipline is pursued pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond within forty days (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty days, a response opposing, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1), the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of mailing/delivery (certified mail receipt, delivery date) is noted; failure to file a response within the 40-day period may result in a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact and that reciprocal discipline is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for imposing exclusion: no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and that exclusion is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, Respondent's failure to file a response led to the determination that (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and (2) exclusion of Respondent is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical violation basis: 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b) via 10.23(c)(5)(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion was ordered for violation of the ethical standard set out in 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5)(i), as evidenced by being disbarred on consent from practice of law in the State of Maryland on ethical grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state disbarment on ethical grounds can constitute a basis for USPTO discipline under the cited ethical provisions and implementing regulation 10.23(c)(5)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for discipline (35 U.S.C. § 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions involving practitioners are grounded in these statutes/regulations; the Order cites this authority as the basis for imposing exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly defines the coverage of the exclusion (patent, trademark, and other non-patent law cases before the USPTO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement: Official Gazette and OED Reading Room posting
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette; disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes a specific draft NOTICE OF EXCLUSION for publication and references the OED Reading Room URL for public access to disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED DGC shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires affirmative notice to state disciplinary authorities and courts as part of the discipline's dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural proof of service/mailing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail (receipt no. 70113500000314475519) and delivered to Respondent on a specified date (June 5, 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate proof of mailing and delivery dates are used to establish that the respondent received the required notice and the 40-day response period began; this supports the procedural validity of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating/contextual factors considered in the Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order records that Respondent was not criminally charged, recognized his wrongful conduct, voluntarily terminated his participation, and cooperated in a DOJ investigation that led to indictment and conviction of co-conspirators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Order imposes exclusion, these factual statements serve as mitigating/contextual information about the nature of the misconduct and the respondent's cooperation; such factors may be referenced in disciplinary determinations or Notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to direct further relief
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order directs 'such other and further relief as the nature of this cause shall require.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director retains discretion to order additional relief beyond the specified exclusion/publication/notice if circumstances warrant.
